description:
## What does the pull request do?

As #3590 describes, placing a resource that itself uses a `{DynamicResouce}` in a `Style.Resources` or `Styles.Resources` caused the dynamic resource to not take effect.

This was because the parent `Styles` object wasn't informing added child styles when resources change, and of course resources can change for a `Style` when is added as a child of a `Styles` object.

Bonus change: make `StyledElement.Styles` readonly. It was already readonly in Application and I can't see a reason it should be writable here. I think this is a remnant of very early code.

## How was the solution implemented (if it's not obvious)?

Call `ISetResourceParent.ParentResourcesChanged` on a style when it is added to a `Styles` collection and when the parent receives a notification that resources have changed. To make this work I had to prevent re-entrancy when notifying of resource changes to prevent stack overflows.

## Checklist

- [x] Added unit tests (if possible)?

## Fixed issues

Fixes #3590

comments.body: What do you think about caching args instance in a static and reusing that? Would save us several thousands allocations when starting the app and loading more complex controls.

Not something that we want to fix within this PR but I wanted to ask if we have any other alternatives to using events for this? We create so many delegates for this that in calendar benchmark it was like the 6th top allocation.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2588062/75100500-7c953a80-55ce-11ea-9d7d-b360fc71e7ac.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2588062/75100506-9cc4f980-55ce-11ea-955a-d2c6538f524c.png)
Yeah we should do that. My vague plan was to indicate which resources changed in the event args, which would mean we can't do that, but for now it's worth doing.
Yeah we could probably remove the usage of events for this.
